markets.label: Gold · XAUUSD
markets.q: Gold XAUUSD spot price
markets.note: Gold often reacts to real yields, the dollar, policy expectations and risk demand. Safe-haven flows can be offset by rising yields or USD strength.

markets.label: Silver · XAGUSD
markets.q: Silver XAGUSD spot price
markets.note: Silver combines precious-metal and industrial demand exposure; its volatility and liquidity can differ materially from Gold.

markets.label: EUR/USD
markets.q: EUR USD exchange rate euro dollar
markets.note: FX is relative: compare both central banks, growth/inflation surprises and yield spreads rather than analysing one currency alone.

markets.label: GBP/USD
markets.q: GBP USD exchange rate sterling dollar
markets.note: Sterling reacts to UK policy and data versus US conditions. UK-specific political/fiscal headlines can change the transmission.

markets.label: USD/JPY
markets.q: USD JPY exchange rate yen dollar
markets.note: The yield differential and central-bank signals often matter, but intervention warnings and rapid carry unwinds can dominate short-term price action.

markets.label: USD/INR
markets.q: USD INR exchange rate RBI India rupee
markets.note: INR can be influenced by oil import costs, dollar conditions, local flows and RBI actions. Confirm contract/venue eligibility with authorised sources.

markets.label: US Dollar Index · DXY
markets.q: US Dollar Index DXY
markets.note: DXY is a currency benchmark, not a currency pair. Its composition and weights matter; strength does not mechanically force every asset lower.

markets.label: US 2-Year Treasury Yield
markets.q: US 2 year Treasury yield bond market
markets.note: Short yields are especially sensitive to expected policy rates. Yield up usually means bond price down, but broader asset reactions depend on why yields moved.

markets.label: US 10-Year Treasury Yield
markets.q: US 10 year Treasury yield yield curve
markets.note: The 10-year reflects expected short rates plus term premium and other factors. Distinguish a growth-led rise from an inflation/fiscal-risk rise.

markets.label: US 30-Year Treasury Yield
markets.q: US 30 year Treasury yield long bond
markets.note: Long bonds are sensitive to long-run inflation, supply/demand and term premium; duration risk can be substantial.

markets.label: S&P 500
markets.q: S&P 500 index stocks market
markets.note: Index direction combines earnings, rates, breadth and concentration. A few mega-caps can hide weak underlying breadth.

markets.label: Nasdaq-100
markets.q: Nasdaq 100 index technology growth stocks
markets.note: Long-duration growth stocks can be rate-sensitive, but earnings growth and positioning may dominate. Track semiconductor and mega-cap earnings separately.

markets.label: VIX Volatility Index
markets.q: Cboe VIX volatility index options
markets.note: VIX is an implied-volatility measure, not a directional index or a directly tradable share. Futures/options have their own term structure and risks.

markets.label: Nifty 50
markets.q: Nifty 50 NSE India index
markets.note: Indian equities combine earnings and global risk with INR, crude, domestic flows and index composition. Verify exchange notices and holidays.

markets.label: Nifty Bank
markets.q: Nifty Bank index Indian banks
markets.note: Bank indices are sensitive to rate transmission, deposit costs, loan growth and credit quality—not just the policy-rate decision.

markets.label: DAX · Germany
markets.q: DAX Germany stock index
markets.note: European equity performance can respond to ECB expectations, industrial cycle, energy costs and currency moves.

markets.label: Nikkei 225 · Japan
markets.q: Nikkei 225 Japan stock index
markets.note: Export sensitivity and the yen can create meaningful cross-asset effects; track local-market hours and overnight US developments.

markets.label: WTI Crude Oil
markets.q: WTI crude oil futures price
markets.note: Oil prices reflect both physical balances and risk premium. An inventory draw can be bullish in one context and irrelevant if already expected.

markets.label: Brent Crude
markets.q: Brent crude oil futures price
markets.note: Brent has a global benchmark role; compare regional supply, freight/insurance risk and product-market spreads.

markets.label: Natural Gas
markets.q: Natural gas futures price storage weather
markets.note: Gas markets are highly regional and weather/seasonality sensitive. A contract benchmark may not reflect local retail gas prices.

markets.label: Copper
markets.q: Copper futures price LME inventory China demand
markets.note: Copper is often used as an industrial-cycle gauge, but inventory location, supply disruptions, currency and positioning can change the signal.

markets.label: Aluminium
markets.q: Aluminium price LME warehouse inventory
markets.note: Aluminium is energy-intensive; power pricing, production restrictions and regional inventory flows can affect premiums and futures.

markets.label: Lithium / Battery Materials
markets.q: lithium prices battery materials supply demand
markets.note: Not every battery material has a liquid retail-tradable contract. Many prices are specialist assessments or private/physical agreements.

markets.label: Bitcoin · BTC
markets.q: Bitcoin BTC crypto price ETF flows derivatives
markets.note: Crypto can trade 24/7 and react to liquidity, leverage and market-structure events. Exchange deposits alone do not prove an intent to sell.

markets.label: Ethereum · ETH
markets.q: Ethereum ETH crypto price network fees ETF flows
markets.note: Ethereum price may respond to broader crypto risk, network economics, product flows and supply dynamics. Verify chain and asset-specific facts.

markets.label: Solana · SOL
markets.q: Solana SOL crypto price DEX volume unlocks
markets.note: DEX activity and high social attention do not guarantee token value accrual; verify liquidity, concentration, unlocks and technical risks.

markets.label: XRP
markets.q: XRP crypto price regulation exchange flows
markets.note: Legal headlines need primary documents and precise scope. Social narratives can overstate the practical effect of a court or regulator update.

markets.label: NVIDIA · NVDA
markets.q: NVIDIA NVDA earnings guidance AI chip stocks
markets.note: For single stocks, compare reported results with consensus, guidance, estimate revisions and what the price already reflects.

markets.label: Apple · AAPL
markets.q: Apple AAPL earnings iPhone demand China
markets.note: Single-stock catalysts include results, guidance, product cycle, legal/regulatory events and market positioning. Use issuer IR filings.

markets.label: Tesla · TSLA
markets.q: Tesla TSLA deliveries earnings margins EV demand
markets.note: Delivery reports, margins and official guidance may affect the thesis; social claims about autonomy or private deals require strong verification.

markets.label: Reliance Industries · NSE
markets.q: Reliance Industries NSE results retail telecom refining
markets.note: Use NSE/BSE disclosures and issuer IR; segment results may have different drivers and market expectations.

markets.label: HDFC Bank · NSE
markets.q: HDFC Bank results deposits loan growth NIM
markets.note: For banks, analyse deposit mix/costs, credit growth and asset quality together instead of relying on one headline.

markets.label: Coffee Futures
markets.q: coffee futures Brazil crop weather price
markets.note: Coffee can respond to crop/weather shocks and logistics; seasonal headlines need confirmation from supply and inventory data.

markets.label: Wheat Futures
markets.q: wheat futures crop weather Black Sea exports
markets.note: Crop reports and export policy matter, but prices also reflect inventories, seasonality and global substitution among origins.

markets.label: Corn Futures
markets.q: corn futures USDA crop yield ethanol exports
markets.note: Corn reacts to crop estimates, weather windows and demand. Distinguish futures benchmark price from local physical basis.

markets.label: Cocoa Futures
markets.q: cocoa futures Ivory Coast crop weather grindings
markets.note: Cocoa supply is geographically concentrated, so local crop or logistics headlines can matter; confirm through industry and exchange data.

markets.label: USD/CHF
markets.q: USD CHF exchange rate Swiss franc
markets.note: CHF often reacts to relative rates and safe-haven demand; the response depends on event geography and policy context.

markets.label: AUD/USD
markets.q: AUD USD exchange rate Australian dollar
markets.note: AUD is sensitive to domestic policy and China/commodity demand, but relative yields and broader risk appetite also matter.

markets.label: USD/CAD
markets.q: USD CAD exchange rate Canadian dollar crude oil
markets.note: Oil can affect CAD through terms-of-trade channels, but rate spreads, domestic data and USD direction also influence the pair.

markets.label: NZD/USD
markets.q: NZD USD exchange rate New Zealand dollar
markets.note: NZD combines local central-bank expectations with Asia-linked demand and global risk appetite.

markets.label: EUR/GBP
markets.q: EUR GBP exchange rate ECB Bank of England
markets.note: Cross-currency pairs are relative trades: compare both economies, data surprises and central-bank pricing.

markets.label: EUR/JPY
markets.q: EUR JPY exchange rate ECB Bank of Japan
markets.note: Carry and yield differentials may be important, but sharp risk-off episodes and policy surprises can unwind positioning quickly.

markets.label: GBP/JPY
markets.q: GBP JPY exchange rate sterling yen
markets.note: Often a volatile cross; combine yield differentials with risk sentiment and volatility rather than assuming it only follows carry.

markets.label: AUD/JPY
markets.q: AUD JPY exchange rate carry trade
markets.note: AUD/JPY is often treated as risk-sensitive, but that relationship can change during policy shocks or commodity-specific moves.

markets.label: EUR/AUD
markets.q: EUR AUD exchange rate ECB RBA
markets.note: Compare Europe and Australia data relative to expectations; commodity and China signals can affect the AUD side.

markets.label: GBP/AUD
markets.q: GBP AUD exchange rate Bank of England RBA
markets.note: A relative macro pair; local surprises can dominate if they materially change expected policy paths.

markets.label: USD/MXN
markets.q: USD MXN exchange rate Mexico peso
markets.note: Higher carry does not remove FX gap risk; policy, trade and risk-off developments can cause abrupt moves.

markets.label: USD/ZAR
markets.q: USD ZAR exchange rate South African rand
markets.note: ZAR can be highly sensitive to global risk sentiment and commodity exposures alongside local structural and policy factors.

markets.label: USD/TRY
markets.q: USD TRY exchange rate Turkish lira inflation central bank
markets.note: Policy framework, inflation, reserves and access restrictions matter; price feeds and tradability differ across venues.

markets.label: USD/CNH
markets.q: USD CNH offshore yuan exchange rate China
markets.note: Offshore CNH and onshore CNY are different market references. Use the right symbol and session for the instrument under study.

markets.label: EUR/INR
markets.q: EUR INR exchange rate euro rupee NSE
markets.note: Cross rates inherit both currency legs; confirm the actual exchange-listed contract and its trading hours.

markets.label: GBP/INR
markets.q: GBP INR exchange rate pound rupee
markets.note: GBP/INR can move through both GBP/USD and USD/INR; use the actual listed instrument and contract specifications.

markets.label: JPY/INR
markets.q: JPY INR exchange rate yen rupee
markets.note: Cross-rate mechanics matter: compare USD/JPY and USD/INR alongside local market quotes.

markets.label: Germany 10-Year Bund Yield
markets.q: Germany 10 year Bund yield
markets.note: Sovereign yields are market-specific. Compare Bunds with other countries using the same maturity and yield convention.

markets.label: UK 10-Year Gilt Yield
markets.q: UK 10 year Gilt yield Bank of England
markets.note: UK gilt yields reflect policy expectations plus term premium, fiscal/issuance expectations and global duration conditions.

markets.label: India 10-Year Government Bond Yield
markets.q: India 10 year government bond yield RBI
markets.note: Domestic yields depend on inflation, RBI liquidity/policy, supply and institutional demand. Check current RBI/FBIL/official market source data.

markets.label: FTSE 100 · UK
markets.q: FTSE 100 index UK stocks
markets.note: FTSE sector composition and foreign revenue exposure mean its drivers can differ from the domestic UK economy.

markets.label: Hang Seng · Hong Kong
markets.q: Hang Seng Index Hong Kong China stocks
markets.note: China policy, property risks, listings and offshore capital flows can all matter; verify announcements from HKEX/company filings.

markets.label: Euro Stoxx 50
markets.q: Euro Stoxx 50 index Europe equities
markets.note: A major euro-area equity benchmark; consider country/sector mix and currency effects when comparing returns.

markets.label: Platinum
markets.q: Platinum futures price supply demand South Africa
markets.note: Platinum has distinct industrial and supply drivers. Do not use Gold as a direct proxy for its fundamentals.

markets.label: Palladium
markets.q: Palladium futures price auto catalyst supply Russia South Africa
markets.note: Automotive demand, substitution with platinum and concentrated supply can create different dynamics from Gold and Silver.

markets.label: BNB
markets.q: BNB crypto price exchange token regulatory news
markets.note: Exchange-related tokens can carry platform, regulatory and concentration risks beyond ordinary crypto market risk.

markets.label: Dogecoin · DOGE
markets.q: Dogecoin DOGE price social sentiment liquidity
markets.note: Meme-token attention can be rapidly amplified and reversed. Verify market depth and avoid treating social mentions as value evidence.

markets.label: Cardano · ADA
markets.q: Cardano ADA crypto price network updates
markets.note: Protocol updates are not automatically price-positive; check user activity, actual adoption and release status.

markets.label: Chainlink · LINK
markets.q: Chainlink LINK crypto price integrations staking
markets.note: Partnership headlines should be checked for what is live, what is planned and whether token demand changes materially.

markets.label: Meta Platforms · META
markets.q: Meta Platforms META earnings ad revenue AI capex
markets.note: Compare ad demand, capex, margins and forward guidance to consensus; increased spending may be interpreted differently by timeframe.

markets.label: Microsoft · MSFT
markets.q: Microsoft MSFT earnings cloud Azure AI capex
markets.note: Cloud growth and AI investment returns are separate questions; compare reported growth with capex and guidance.

markets.label: AMD · Advanced Micro Devices
markets.q: AMD earnings data center chips AI GPU market
markets.note: Sector sympathy can be strong, but track company-specific product, margin and guidance details rather than reading only a competitor headline.

markets.label: Soybean Futures
markets.q: soybean futures USDA South America crop exports
markets.note: Crop balances, export sales and crush margins are central; production estimates and actual shipment data can diverge.

markets.label: Sugar Futures
markets.q: sugar futures Brazil ethanol India export policy
markets.note: Sugar prices link agricultural supply to energy economics in key producer regions; policy changes should be confirmed with official notices.

markets.label: Cotton Futures
markets.q: cotton futures USDA crop demand textile exports
markets.note: Cotton combines crop/weather risk with textile demand and inventory; futures price differs from local physical basis.

markets.label: Global Freight / Baltic Dry
markets.q: Baltic Dry Index freight rates shipping
markets.note: Freight indices and freight futures are specialist markets; verify index definition, route coverage, liquidity and contract settlement.

markets.label: EU Carbon Allowances
markets.q: EU carbon allowance price EUA emissions futures
markets.note: Carbon allowance prices depend on scheme rules, cap/supply and energy economics. Product eligibility and regional rules are specific.
